text: A civil appeal is a legal process by which a party challenges a lower court's decision in a civil matter before a higher court.
Jurisdiction is the authority of a court to hear and decide a case, including territorial and subject-matter jurisdiction.
The party who files an appeal against a court decision.
The party against whom an appeal is filed.
A written complaint filed in a civil court stating the cause of action.
The defendant's formal reply to the plaint.
A reply filed by the plaintiff to the defendant's written statement.
A formal expression of a civil court's final decision determining rights of parties.
The reasoning provided by a judge explaining the decision.
Rejection of a case by a court without granting relief.
Legal reasons on which a judgment is challenged in a higher court.
Material presented in court to prove or disprove facts.
A formal communication informing a party of a legal claim or demand.
A civil suit filed to recover money owed.
Additional amount payable on a principal sum, often awarded by courts.
A document attached to a legal filing as supporting evidence.
A court order requiring a party to appear and respond to a case.
The legally prescribed time limit for filing a case or appeal.
Fees paid to the court for filing legal proceedings.
A declaration confirming that the contents of a legal document are true.
The set of facts that give rise to a legal claim.
The remedy sought by a party from the court.
The court of first instance where a case is initially heard.
A court that reviews decisions of lower courts.
The obligation to prove allegations in a case.
The level of certainty required to prove a case (preponderance in civil cases).
Questioning of a witness by the opposing party.
A written statement sworn under oath used as evidence.
The process of enforcing a court's decree.
A court order temporarily suspending enforcement of a judgment.
A court order directing a party to do or refrain from doing something.
Expenses awarded by the court to compensate a party for litigation.
Formal written statements of claims and defenses.
Initial testimony given by a witness.
Evidence in the form of documents.
Evidence given verbally by witnesses in court.
A statement acknowledging a fact as true.
A statement rejecting an allegation made by the opposing party.
A point of dispute between parties that the court must decide.
A decision by the court on a particular issue.
A legal principle established in earlier cases that courts follow.
The legal reasoning forming the basis of a judgment.
Remarks made by a judge that are not essential to the decision.
The means by which a court enforces a right or compensates a loss.
A legally binding agreement between parties.
Failure to perform obligations under a contract.
Monetary compensation awarded for loss or injury.
A court order requiring a party to fulfill contractual obligations.
A contractual obligation to compensate for loss.
A dispute resolution method where parties submit to a neutral arbitrator for a binding decision.
A legal contract by which a landlord grants a tenant the right to occupy property for a specified period in exchange for rent.
The landlord or owner who grants a lease to a tenant.
The tenant who receives the right to occupy property under a lease agreement.
Periodic payment made by a tenant to a landlord for the use of property.
An amount paid by a tenant to a landlord as security against damage or unpaid rent, refundable at the end of tenancy.
The legal process by which a landlord removes a tenant from the property.
A formal notice issued by a landlord requiring a tenant to vacate the premises.
The legal right to occupy property owned by another person, typically under a lease or rental agreement.
Unpaid rent that is overdue and owed by a tenant to a landlord.
When a tenant rents out all or part of the leased property to another person with or without landlord's permission.
An agreement under which a licensor grants a licensee permission to use premises for a fixed period without creating a tenancy.
A person who has been granted a licence to occupy or use premises.
The owner who grants a licence to another person to use their property.
Physical control or occupancy of a property.
Delivery of a property free from any occupants or encumbrances to the new owner or tenant.
Profits or compensation recoverable from a person who has wrongfully occupied property after their right to possession has ended.
A legal action to recover possession of land or property from an occupant.
Statutory regulation limiting the amount a landlord may charge for renting out property, governed by state Rent Control Acts in India.
The maximum rent fixed under rent control legislation that a landlord is permitted to charge.
A tenancy that may be terminated at any time by either the landlord or tenant without notice.
A legal document that transfers ownership of immovable property from seller to buyer upon receipt of full consideration.
The legal transfer of property title from one person to another.
A transfer of interest in property to a lender as security for repayment of a loan.
The borrower who pledges property as security for a loan.
The lender who holds the mortgage on the property as security.
A claim, lien, or liability attached to a property that may affect its transfer.
A legal document proving ownership of property.
The process of recording a legal document with the government authority to give it legal validity, mandatory for property transactions above a threshold value.
A tax levied by the state government on legal documents including property transactions, calculated as a percentage of property value.
A legal document authorizing one person to act on behalf of another in legal or financial matters.
The division of jointly owned property among co-owners, either by mutual agreement or court order.
A person who shares ownership of property with one or more other persons.
A form of co-ownership where all owners have equal rights and the right of survivorship.
A form of co-ownership where each owner holds a distinct share that can be transferred independently.
A legal document transferring ownership of property voluntarily without any consideration.
A legal declaration of a person's wishes regarding the distribution of their property after death.
The legal process of proving a will is valid and administering the estate of a deceased person.
The legal process by which a person's property passes to heirs after death.
Dying without a valid will, in which case property is distributed according to personal law.
The legal right to inherit property from a deceased person.
Financial support ordered by a court to be paid by one party to another, typically in matrimonial or family disputes.
Periodic financial support paid by one spouse to another after separation or divorce.
The legal dissolution of a marriage by a court.
Dissolution of marriage by agreement of both spouses under Section 13B of the Hindu Marriage Act or Section 28 of the Special Marriage Act.
The legal right and responsibility to care for and make decisions about a child.
A temporary court order made during the pendency of proceedings to maintain the status quo or provide urgent relief.
A court proceeding or order made in the absence of one party.
A formal notice filed in court requesting that no action be taken without informing the person who filed it.
Willful disobedience or disrespect of a court order or authority.
A court decree passed on the basis of a settlement reached between the parties during litigation.
A written contract between landlord and tenant specifying terms of rental including rent amount, duration, and obligations of both parties.
The owner of property who lets it out to a tenant in exchange for rent.
A person who occupies property owned by another under a rental or lease agreement.
The fixed amount payable by a tenant to the landlord every month for use of the premises.
An amount paid by the tenant at the start of tenancy, returnable upon vacating the premises subject to deductions for damages.
Periodic charges paid for upkeep and maintenance of common areas and building facilities, typically collected by the housing society.
A pre-agreed percentage by which monthly rent is escalated each year, typically 5-10% in Indian residential agreements.
A fine imposed on the tenant for failure to pay rent within the stipulated due date, usually charged per day of delay.
A clause restricting use of the leased premises exclusively for living and prohibiting any commercial activity.
Major repairs to the core structure of a building which are the responsibility of the landlord and not the tenant.
The tenant's right to use and enjoy the rented premises without interference or disturbance from the landlord.
The landlord's right to inspect the premises with prior notice, typically 24-48 hours in advance.
A written notice given by either party to end a rental agreement, typically 30 days in advance.
Payment of rent via electronic bank transfer as specified in the rental agreement.
The mechanism agreed upon to resolve conflicts arising from the agreement, including negotiation and recourse to competent court.
The law applicable to a contract, in this context the law of the State of Maharashtra.
A person who signs a legal document to attest that the parties signed it in their presence.
Bye-laws and regulations of a housing cooperative society that the tenant is obligated to follow.
The net usable floor area of an apartment excluding the area covered by walls, as measured in square feet or square meters.
The court having proper jurisdiction to adjudicate disputes arising from the agreement, typically the District Court of the relevant city.
In a lease or rent agreement, the lessor is the landlord (पट्टादाता) who grants the property on rent. Must NOT be translated as beneficiary or labharthi.
In a lease or rent agreement, the lessee is the tenant (पट्टेदार) who takes the property on rent.
Also called किरायानामा or भाड़ा पट्टा करार in Hindi. A contract between landlord and tenant for residential tenancy.
Called सुरक्षा जमा राशि in Hindi. Refundable amount paid by tenant to landlord at start of tenancy.
Called शांतिपूर्ण कब्जा in Hindi legal usage. The tenant's right to peaceful occupation without landlord interference.
The written document prepared by the police on receiving information about a cognizable offence, which sets the criminal law in motion.
Short form of First Information Report, registered under Section 154 of the CrPC, now Section 173 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023.
An FIR that can be registered at any police station regardless of where the offence occurred, and is later transferred to the police station having jurisdiction.
An offence for which the police can register an FIR and arrest without a warrant, such as murder or theft.
An offence for which the police cannot arrest without a warrant and need a magistrate's permission to investigate.
Release of an accused person from custody pending trial, usually on furnishing a bond or surety to ensure appearance in court.
A direction by the Sessions Court or High Court that a person be released on bail if arrested, sought by someone who apprehends arrest for a non-bailable offence.
An offence in which the accused has a legal right to be released on bail.
An offence in which bail is not a matter of right and is granted at the discretion of the court.
An offence that the complainant may settle with the accused, with or without the court's permission, resulting in acquittal.
A written undertaking by the accused, with or without sureties, to appear before the court when required, failing which a stated amount is forfeited.
A person who takes responsibility for an accused's appearance in court and is liable to pay a stated amount if the accused fails to appear.
The final report filed by the police in court after investigation, stating the offences and evidence against the accused.
The stage at which the court formally records the offences the accused will be tried for, after finding sufficient grounds to proceed.
The act of a court formally taking judicial notice of an offence in order to begin proceedings.
A court order sending an accused into police custody or judicial custody during investigation.
Detention of an accused by the police for interrogation under a magistrate's order, for a period limited by law.
Detention of an accused in jail under the control of the magistrate, where the police cannot interrogate without the court's permission.
A written order issued by a court authorising the police to arrest a person, search a place or seize property.
A warrant under which the arrested person must be produced before the court and cannot be released on bail by the police.
A person declared by the court to be absconding to avoid arrest, whose property may be attached.
A court's decision that the accused is not guilty of the offence charged.
A court's finding that the accused is guilty of the offence charged.
Release of the accused by the court before trial because there are insufficient grounds to proceed.
The punishment imposed by the court on a convicted person.
Release of a convicted offender under supervision instead of imprisonment, subject to good conduct.
Temporary release of a prisoner for a specific period or purpose, after which the prisoner returns to serve the remaining sentence.
A process in which the accused pleads guilty in exchange for a lesser sentence, available for offences punishable with imprisonment of up to seven years.
A shortened trial procedure for minor offences, with a simplified record of proceedings.
The setting aside of an FIR or criminal proceedings by the High Court, usually in exercise of its inherent powers.
Instigating, conspiring in, or intentionally aiding the commission of an offence.
An agreement between two or more persons to do an illegal act, or a legal act by illegal means.
Causing death with the intention or knowledge that the act is likely to cause death; murder is an aggravated form of culpable homicide.
The guilty mind or criminal intention required for most offences.
The physical act or omission that constitutes an offence.
A writ directing a person or authority holding someone in custody to produce that person before the court, so the lawfulness of the detention can be examined.
A writ ordering a public authority to perform a legal duty it has failed to perform.
A writ by which a higher court quashes an order of a lower court or tribunal passed without jurisdiction or in violation of law.
A writ issued by a higher court to stop a lower court or tribunal from acting beyond its jurisdiction.
A writ requiring a person holding a public office to show by what legal authority they hold it.
A petition filed in a High Court under Article 226 or in the Supreme Court under Article 32 of the Constitution seeking enforcement of rights.
A case filed in court to protect the public interest, which any person may file even if not directly affected.
Basic rights guaranteed to individuals under Part III of the Constitution of India, enforceable in the courts.
A petition to the Supreme Court under Article 136 of the Constitution seeking permission to appeal against a judgment of any court or tribunal in India.
A petition asking the same court to reconsider its own judgment on limited grounds, such as an error apparent on the face of the record.
A petition asking a higher court to examine the legality or correctness of an order of a subordinate court where no appeal lies.
A final remedy before the Supreme Court, available after dismissal of a review petition, to correct a gross miscarriage of justice.
Action taken by a court on its own initiative, without a formal petition by any party.
The right of a party to bring a case before a court.
The principle that a matter finally decided by a competent court cannot be litigated again between the same parties.
A matter pending before a court, which should not be commented on in a way that may prejudice the proceedings.
On first view; evidence sufficient to establish a fact unless it is disproved.
In good faith, without intention to deceive.
In bad faith, with dishonest intent.
Among other things.
The existing state of affairs, which a court often orders to be maintained until further hearing.
Afresh or from the beginning, as in a fresh trial or hearing.
Basic principles of fair procedure, including the right to be heard and the rule against bias.
The principle that no person should be condemned without being given a fair hearing.
A document by which a party authorises an advocate to appear and act on their behalf in court.
Postponement of a court hearing to a later date.
An application filed while a case is pending, seeking an interim direction or relief.
An injunction granted while a suit is pending, to preserve the position until the final decision, under Order XXXIX of the Code of Civil Procedure.
An injunction granted by a final decree that permanently restrains a party from doing a particular act.
A suit under Order XXXVII of the Code of Civil Procedure for recovering debts based on written contracts or negotiable instruments, in which the defendant must obtain leave to defend.
A suit seeking a declaration from the court about a legal status or right, under the Specific Relief Act, 1963.
A complaint filed before a Consumer Commission alleging defective goods, deficient services or unfair trade practices.
Any fault, shortcoming or inadequacy in the quality or manner of a service that is required to be maintained by law or under a contract.
A deceptive or unfair method used to promote the sale of goods or services, such as false advertising.
Return of a cheque unpaid by the bank; when it is due to insufficient funds, it can be an offence under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881.
A written document such as a cheque, promissory note or bill of exchange that promises payment and can be transferred to another person.
A written, signed, unconditional promise to pay a certain sum of money to a specified person or to the bearer.
A person who promises to pay a debt or perform an obligation if the principal debtor fails to do so.
A pre-agreed amount stated in a contract, payable as compensation in case of breach.
A contract clause excusing a party from performance due to extraordinary events beyond its control, such as natural disasters or war.
Something of value given by each party in return for the other's promise, required for a valid contract.
An agreement that is not enforceable by law.
A contract that is enforceable but may be set aside at the option of one party, for example because of coercion or fraud.
Discharge of a contract when performance becomes impossible due to an unforeseen event beyond the parties' control.
Replacement of an existing contract with a new one, with the consent of all parties.
A document recording the terms agreed between parties, which may or may not be legally binding depending on its terms.
A contract in which the parties agree not to disclose specified confidential information.
The final decision of an arbitrator or arbitral tribunal, enforceable in the same manner as a decree of court.
A neutral person appointed to decide a dispute in arbitration.
A voluntary dispute resolution process in which a neutral mediator helps the parties reach a settlement.
A dispute resolution process in which a conciliator assists the parties and may propose terms of settlement.
A forum for amicable settlement of disputes, whose award is final and binding with no appeal against it.
A public officer authorised to attest and certify documents and administer oaths.
The signing of a document by witnesses to confirm that it was executed in their presence.
The person who makes and signs an affidavit.
The change of the owner's name in the revenue records of a property after a transfer, used for tax purposes; it is not proof of title.
A certificate from the sub-registrar's office listing registered transactions on a property, used to check whether it is free of legal liabilities.
A land record in Maharashtra, also called Satbara Utara, showing ownership, cultivation and rights details of agricultural land.
A right to use another person's land for a specific purpose, such as a right of way.
Acquisition of title to property through continuous, open and hostile possession for the period fixed by law, which is twelve years for private land.
A right to retain possession of another person's property until a debt is paid.
Creation of a charge on movable property as security for a loan, where the borrower keeps possession of the property.
Delivery of goods as security for payment of a debt or performance of a promise.
A certificate issued by the local authority confirming that a building is fit for occupation and was built according to approved plans.
A remedy in which a court directs a spouse who has withdrawn from the company of the other without reasonable excuse to resume cohabitation.
A court decree permitting spouses to live apart without dissolving the marriage.
The legal authority to care for the person or property of a minor.
An order under the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 restraining a person from committing acts of domestic violence.
The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (BNS), which replaced the Indian Penal Code with effect from 1 July 2024.
The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS), which replaced the Code of Criminal Procedure with effect from 1 July 2024.
The Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA), which replaced the Indian Evidence Act, 1872 with effect from 1 July 2024.
The Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 (CPC), which governs procedure in civil courts in India.
A certificate issued by revenue authorities identifying the legal heirs of a deceased person.
A certificate issued by a civil court authorising heirs to collect debts and securities owed to a deceased person.
A grant by a court authorising a person to administer the estate of someone who died without a will, or whose will names no executor.
The person named in a will to carry out its instructions.
A person who makes a will.
A document that adds to, changes or revokes parts of an existing will.
